title: Tuition fees for Students from non-EU states
text:
FAU charges tuition fees per semester for students from non-EU states who enroll at FAU for the first time or change subjects from summer semester 2027.
On this page you will find all the information on tuition fees for non-EU students. Specific information relating to your own application and your obligation to pay tuition fees is always available in your profile in the campo portal.
Tuition fees – an investment in academic success
Tuition fees will help maintain and further develop attractive study conditions and competitive infrastructure for studying and teaching at FAU. Our goal is to provide international students with the best possible prerequisites for academic success at FAU from the outset. Students who are required to pay tuition fees will be guaranteed a place in a German course free of charge and will also benefit from a comprehensive welcome package, ranging from welcome and onboarding programs organized by the Student Advice Center and study advisors at the faculties to counseling services.

Prerequisites for collecting tuition fees
Tuition fees are due each semester for studying at FAU if all of the following prerequisites are met:
You are studying a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree program
You do not have German citizenship, citizenship of an EU member state or citizenship of a contracting state of the Agreement on the European Economic Area (EEA: Norway, Iceland, Lichtenstein)
You do not have a German university entrance qualification
You do not have established ties to Germany
Using the fee finder, you can quickly check whether you are required to pay tuition fees for studying at FAU.
Irrespective of tuition fees, all students are required to pay a semester contribution (Student Services contribution) This currently amounts to 82 euros per semester.
Amount of tuition fees
The amount of tuition fees depends on the degree program and final qualification and amounts to between 1,000 and 6,000 euros per semester. The amount you are required to pay for your degree program is listed in the following sections, sorted according to faculty and teaching degrees.
Rules for tuition fees for part-time study
Unless stated otherwise, the tuition fees are for full-time study. Tuition fees are halved for part-time study.
Rules for tuition fees in two-subject Bachelor’s degree programs
In the case of the two-subject Bachelor’s degree program at the Faculty of Humanities, Social Sciences, and Theology, tuition fees are only charged for one subject. You are not required to pay double the tuition fees.

General information on tuition fees and legal framework
What is my fee used for?
FAU’s goal is to provide all students with equal opportunities for academic success and to ensure outstanding study and learning conditions on a permanent basis. Against this backdrop, we are introducing tuition fees for students from non-EU states, in accordance with the Bavarian Higher Education Innovation Act (BayHIG, Section 13).
Going forward, all students will contribute to the financing and ongoing improvement of study conditions: Students from non-EU countries via tuition fees, and German and EU students through the funding of the higher education system through taxation.
Who has to pay tuition fees?
Tuition fees for students from non-EU states in Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programs will only be introduced from summer semester 2027 for newly enrolled students and students who are changing subjects.
No tuition fees are due for:
Students from non-EU states who were already enrolled at FAU before summer semester 2027 (unless they are changing subject)
Students in State Examination degree programs
Students in degree programs for professional development
Doctoral candidates (including those on PhD programs)
FAU Scientia students
Exchange and visiting students (in particular ERASMUS)
Students taking module programs and
Other study programs.
Who is exempt from the obligation to pay tuition fees?
All students already enrolled in winter semester 2026/27 and the groups named under Section 13 (3)(2) BayHIG are exempt:
Members of another member state in the European Union
Members of another contracting state of the Agreement on the European Economic Area (member of the EEA but not the EU: Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein)
Individuals who obtained their university entrance qualification in Germany
Individuals with established ties to Germany according to Section 8 paragraphs 1 to 4 of the Federal Training Assistance Act, unless they are already covered by nos. 1 to 3
Individuals who are considered equal to German citizens or are exempt from charges due to further agreements, legal directives or interstate agreements.
The following students are also exempt from paying tuition fees:
Students who are currently on leave of absence
Students with a disability pursuant to Section 2 of the Bavarian Act on the Equal Treatment of Disabled People (Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz, BGG) that severely impacts their ability to study
International students in asylum proceedings with temporary permission to stay pursuant to Section 55 AsyGl and citizenship of a country assessed by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees on the basis of the declaration from the Federal Minister of the Interior as having a protected quota of 50% or more (exemption upon request for the duration of the proceedings)
Are any scholarships or waivers available?
Yes. Information on scholarships and waivers will soon be available on our website.
What applies to applicants with dual EU/EEC citizenship?
This application fee is not charged for applicants with dual EU/EEC nationality.
What is meant by “established ties to Germany”?
Students with established ties to Germany are individuals who have been living in Germany for at least five years before beginning a degree program and who have been in legal employment during this time or who have at least one parent who has been living in Germany during three of the last six years and who was in legal employment during this time.
Am I required to pay tuition fees for my Master’s degree program if I completed my Bachelor’s degree at FAU?
If you obtained a Bachelor’s degree from FAU, you are exempt from paying tuition fees for the consecutive Master’s degree program. This is subject to the condition that you complete your Bachelor’s degree program successfully before commencing the Master’s degree program.
In order to avoid paying tuition fees, you must prove that you have completed your Bachelor’s degree at the latest five weeks after lectures start.
Am I required to pay tuition fees for my Master’s degree program if I completed my Bachelor’s degree at another university in Germany?
If you obtained a Bachelor’s degree from a German university, you are generally exempt from paying tuition fees for the Master’s degree program. This is subject to the condition that you complete your Bachelor’s degree program successfully before commencing the Master’s degree program.
Can I apply for an exemption?
Students who are currently on leave of absence are exempt from the obligation to pay tuition fees for the duration of their leave of absence.
Students with a disability pursuant to Section 2 of the Bavarian Act on the Equal Treatment of Disabled People (Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz, BGG) that severely impacts their ability to study can apply for exemption by submitting proof of their disability. This is then checked on a case by case basis.
International students in asylum proceedings with temporary permission to stay pursuant to Section 55 AsyGl and citizenship of a country assessed by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees on the basis of the declaration from the Federal Minister of the Interior as having a protected quota of 50% or more are exempt from paying tuition fees upon request and for the duration of the proceedings.
How much are tuition fees for non-EU students?
The amount of tuition fees depends on the degree program. The tuition fees for your degree program are stated above.
As a rule, tuition fees for
Bachelor’s degree programs are 1,000, 2,000 or 3,000 euros per semester
Master’s degree programs are 2,000, 4,000 or 6,000 euros per semester
Studying two degree programs: If you are enrolled in two degree programs at one time, you must pay tuition fees for both degree programs.
The regular semester contribution is due irrespective of tuition fees.
Are my tuition fees refunded if I cannot commence studies after all?
In the case of de-registration within four weeks of the start of the semester, any tuition fees that have been paid can be reimbursed upon application. Reimbursement is not possible for de-registration at a later date.
How to pay the fee
How and where can I pay the fee?
The fee is paid via ePayBayern, the e-payment platform of the Free State of Bavaria.
Where can I find my payment notification?
The payment notification is made available electronically via the campo user account. You receive a message about the payment notification during the application process as well as by email after it has been uploaded.
How do I know how much I have to pay?
The amount of the fee is stated in the payment notification. This is made available in your campo user account.
Which payment methods are accepted?
Payment via PayPal or credit card (Visa/Mastercard) is accepted.
Can I pay the fee even if I don’t have a European payment method?
Payment is accepted in Euros only. The rules of the payment service provider (PayPal, Visa, MasterCard) apply regarding the exchange rate and fees.
What is the deadline for payment?
Tuition fees are due upon enrollment and must be paid via ePayment at the latest ten working days after the payment notification has been received.
How long does it take for the payment to appear in campo?
After successful completion of the payment via ePayBayern, it takes 3-10 working days for the payment to appear in campo. The enrollment will not be processed until payment has been received.
How can I find out if my payment has arrived at FAU?
As soon as your payment has appeared in campo, you will receive a payment confirmation (PDF) and a notification via email.
What happens if the payment is not made or it arrives too late?
If the payment is not made within ten working days after the payment notification has been received, the enrollment will not be processed. This also applies if the payment cannot clearly be allocated to a specific enrollment request.
Who do I contact if I have problems with making the payment on ePayBayern?
Please contact ePayBayern via email at ePayment@lff.bayern.de if you have any problems with the payment.
Please note that it cannot answer any questions related to the enrollment request in campo and the obligation to pay the fee, as ePayBayern is a payment service provider and has no knowledge about the reason for the payment (amount, reason, deadlines, and so on).
